ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Given: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AD$ is the altitude from $A$ to side $BC$. There is an inscribed rectangle $PQMN$ within this triangle, one side of the rectangle lies on $BC$, and the other two vertices are on $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. If $BC=100$, $AD=40$, and $PQ=PN$ with $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, directly provide the value of $BN\cdot CM$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the vertex A of triangle ABC is above, and BC is the base; AD is perpendicular from A to the base BC, with foot D. Rectangle PQMN is inscribed in the triangle, N and M are on BC, P is on AB, Q is on AC, PQ is parallel to BC, PN and QM are vertical; AD intersects PQ at E. Then reason: Let s=PQ=PN. The top side PQ of the rectangle is parallel to BC, and its height from BC is s, so the length of the cross-section line where the top side lies and the whole base satisfy the similar-triangles ratio: PQ=BC·(AD-s)/AD=100·(40-s)/40. Also PQ=s, therefore s=100(40-s)/40, solving gives 40s=4000-100s, 140s=4000, s=200/7. Since the small left right triangle BPN is similar to triangle BDA, BN/PN=BD/AD; since the small right right triangle CMQ is similar to triangle CDA, CM/MQ=DC/AD. Since PN=MQ=s, BN·CM=s^2·(BD·DC)/AD^2. Also because ∠BAC=90°, AD is the altitude to hypotenuse BC in right triangle ABC, so BD·DC=AD^2. Therefore BN·CM=s^2=(200/7)^2=40000/49.
